role_description: Runs AWS Partner Network programme operations, AWS Marketplace listings, private offers, co-sell motions and partner opportunity reporting.
paper_title: AWS Partner Operations & Marketplace Specialist | Assessment Paper

questions.question_text: An ISV wants to transact a negotiated, customer-specific price and payment schedule for its SaaS product through AWS Marketplace. Which mechanism is designed for this?
options: Publishing a second public listing at the discounted price.
Creating a Private Offer for that specific buyer account with agreed pricing, duration and EULA.
Issuing the customer a promotional credit code at checkout.
Asking the customer to purchase at list price and refunding the difference offline.

questions.question_text: In the AWS Partner Network, which statement best describes the purpose of registering an opportunity through APN Customer Engagements (ACE)?
options: It is only a marketing formality with no effect on the deal.
It shares the partner's validated opportunity with AWS to enable co-sell collaboration, AWS seller alignment and programme benefit eligibility.
It transfers ownership of the customer relationship to AWS.
It automatically generates the customer's AWS invoice.

questions.question_text: A SaaS product is being listed on AWS Marketplace with metered usage pricing. Which integration is required for AWS to bill the customer correctly for consumption?
options: The seller emails a monthly usage spreadsheet to AWS Marketplace operations.
The product reports usage records to the AWS Marketplace Metering Service, and entitlements are checked via the Entitlement Service.
Usage is inferred automatically by AWS from CloudTrail with no seller integration.
The customer self-reports usage in the AWS Billing console.

questions.question_text: Which set of items is genuinely required before a new SaaS listing can go live and transact on AWS Marketplace?
options: Only a product logo and a short description.

A registered seller account with tax and bank (disbursement) details, product listing metadata, pricing model, EULA or standard contract, support terms, and a successful buyer-side subscription/fulfilment test.
An AWS Premier Tier partner designation and a signed reseller agreement.
A public AMI and nothing else, since SaaS listings reuse AMI pipelines.

questions.question_text: An ISV has a multi-tenant SaaS analytics product and wants to be transacting on AWS Marketplace within eight weeks. Write the end-to-end onboarding plan you would own as Partner Operations Specialist: the workstreams, key milestones, and the dependencies most likely to delay go-live.
questions.instructions: Write 250-400 words. Present it as a sequenced plan with owners and the realistic blockers.
questions.evaluation_criteria: Strong answers cover: seller registration (AWS Marketplace Management Portal, tax interview, bank/disbursement setup, legal entity checks); product definition (pricing model — contract, subscription, metered, contract-with-consumption; dimensions; free trial); technical integration (SaaS subscription/registration URL, Entitlement and Metering Service, buyer-account resolution token handling); legal (EULA vs. Standard Contract for AWS Marketplace, DPA, support SLA); listing content and AWS listing review cycles; end-to-end test subscription and fulfilment validation; go-live and post-launch reporting. Credit for naming realistic blockers — listing review iterations, tax/banking verification lag, engineering capacity for metering integration, legal redlines — and for a mitigation per blocker. Deduct for vague plans with no technical integration or no legal/finance workstream.

questions.question_text: A large enterprise buyer wants to purchase the ISV's product through AWS Marketplace on negotiated terms: a three-year commitment, a 22% discount off list, annual payments, custom contract language, and drawdown against their AWS commitment. Describe how you would structure and execute this, and what you would verify before it is issued.
questions.instructions: Write 250-400 words. Be operationally specific about the steps and the checks.
questions.evaluation_criteria: Strong answers describe a multi-year Private Offer: confirming the correct buyer AWS account ID, agreeing pricing and dimensions, setting the flexible payment schedule and instalment dates, offer expiry, and attaching the negotiated EULA / amended contract terms. Should verify internal approvals (discount/deal desk sign-off, margin impact, listing fee), that the buyer's procurement is aligned on AWS as the transacting channel, tax and currency considerations, whether the spend counts toward an EDP/commitment, and channel/reseller involvement (CPPO) if a partner resells. Credit for testing/previewing the offer before issuing, tracking acceptance before expiry, and a clear handoff to finance for disbursement reconciliation. Deduct for answers that only say "create a private offer" with no verification or approval steps.

questions.question_text: How would you build and run the co-sell motion between the ISV's sales team and AWS account teams? Describe the process, the data hygiene you would enforce, and how you would measure whether the motion is working.
questions.instructions: Write 250-400 words. Include the operational cadence and the metrics.
questions.evaluation_criteria: Strong answers cover: ACE opportunity submission rules (what qualifies, required fields, validated vs. prospect stage), bi-directional referral handling and SLAs, alignment with AWS Partner Development Manager / Partner Development Rep and AWS account teams, joint account mapping and target-account lists, enablement of the ISV sellers on how to engage AWS sellers, cadence of pipeline reviews, and Marketplace-as-the-transaction-path guidance. Data hygiene: accurate stage and close dates, no duplicate submissions, correct customer account IDs, timely status updates, launched/closed-lost reporting discipline. Metrics: number of ACE-registered opportunities, AWS-originated vs. partner-originated pipeline, win rate, cycle time, Marketplace transacted revenue, co-sell influenced ARR, referral acceptance rate. Deduct for no process detail, no CRM/ACE hygiene, or no measurable outcomes.

questions.question_text: Leadership asks for a monthly AWS partnership operations report. Describe what you would include, where the data comes from, and how you would handle a discrepancy between AWS-reported Marketplace revenue and the ISV's internal finance numbers.
questions.instructions: Write 250-400 words. Address both the reporting design and the reconciliation process.
questions.evaluation_criteria: Strong answers define a report containing: Marketplace transacted revenue and units, active subscriptions and churn, private offers issued/accepted/expired, ACE pipeline by stage and co-sell influenced revenue, programme and funding status (MDF/POC funds, certifications, tier requirements), listing health and review status, and compliance/documentation items due. Sources named: AWS Marketplace seller reports and disbursement reports, Marketplace Management Portal, ACE/Partner Central, internal CRM, finance ledger. Reconciliation: compare at line-item/offer level, account for AWS listing fees, refunds, credits, disbursement timing lag versus revenue recognition, currency and tax withholding, then document root cause and raise an AWS support/Marketplace ops case where genuinely unexplained. Credit for controls preventing recurrence and for clear escalation ownership. Deduct for answers with no data sources or no structured reconciliation approach.
